Reason- Result: Because and Since
You can use because, since or as to talk about the reason and the result of something in one sentence. The result of something is the consequence and the reason is the cause.
Since we added all that extra spice, it has a lot of zesty flavor.

In speaking and writing, there are many times when you will need to give reasons for something. You might also have to provide the causes.
Let's look at how to use different connectives to answer the question “Why did this happen and what was the result?”

because
→ this is the most commonly used connective
→ the result is given first and then the cause
→ the structure that follows is subject – verb - object
→ you could also use as or since in this way

Elena called the plumber because there was a leak under the kitchen sink.
Elena called the plumber since there was a leak under the kitchen sink.
Elena called the plumber as there was a leak under the kitchen sink.
(“Elena called the plumber” is the result. “There was a leak under the kitchen sink” is the cause.)

since
→ when the cause comes first, followed by the result
→ (because can also be used when the reason comes before the consequence)
→ the structure that follows is subject – verb - object

Since the plumber couldn't come, Elena tried to fix the leak herself.
Because the plumber couldn't come, Elena tried to fix the leak herself.
(“The plumber couldn't come” is the cause that led to the result “Elena tried to fix the leak herself”.)

because of + a noun
because of + verb-ing (a possessive usually comes before the verb-ing here)
→ these structures introduce the reason

Unfortunately, the leak got worse because of her lack of plumbing experience.
Unfortunately, the leak got worse because of her trying to fix it without the proper tools.
(“Her lack of plumbing experience” and “her trying to fix it” are the reasons why “the leak got worse”.)
Remember that all of these result clauses are dependent and cannot stand as sentences on their own.
I usually double the amount of spice because vegetarian recipes are often quite bland.
Since cinnamon helps to process sugar, it keeps your blood sugar level low.
I just thought I became unhealthier because of my eating unhealthy food.
Spices and herbs have been valued for centuries as they can treat and prevent illness.
Reporting Statements
You can say in your own words what someone else has said. There are several different reporting verbs that can help you to do this.
I told you that it wouldn't be boring.
You can use a that-clause after most reporting verbs.

Example:
The man agreed that watching television was one of the best ways to relax.

After some verbs, it is necessary to put an object before the that-clause.
Some of these verbs include: inform, notify, convince, tell, assure, remind, reassure and persuade.

Examples:
Luke informed his sister that their parents would be home late.
Hans notified his boss that he had to leave work because of a family emergency.
I told Leia that everything was going to be okay.
For some other verbs like promise, teach, show, warn and advise, it is not always necessary to put an object after the reporting verb.

Example:
I overheard Luke talking with his sister. Luke promised (his sister) that he would pick her up after school.
You convinced me that it would be scrumptious and you were right.
My doctor informed me that certain spices are very good for your health.
My friend convinced me that there are herbs and spices that can help with depression and mood swings too.
He assured me that he feels so much more energetic and positive when he includes certain foods in his diet.

images.text:
Amy: Wow, that vegetable broth soup turned out really well! I told you that it wouldn't be boring.
Peter: Yes, you convinced me that it would be scrumptious and you were right.
Vanessa: Since we added all that extra spice, it has a lot of zesty flavor. I often find that vegetarian dishes need a few more spices and herbs than the recipe calls for. I usually double the amount of spice because vegetarian recipes are often quite bland. You can just keep adding spice and tasting the food until it's exactly the way you want it.
Amy: My doctor informed me that certain spices are very good for your health. What do you know about that, Vanessa?

Vanessa: It's true. Since cinnamon helps to process sugar, it keeps your blood sugar level low. Ginger reduces inflammation and arthritis pain. Some people think that it also fights cancer.
Peter: Really? I had no idea that food could make you healthier. I just thought I became unhealthier because of my eating unhealthy food.
Vanessa: Yes, spices and herbs have been valued for centuries as they can treat and prevent illness. Before modern medicines were developed people relied on these natural sources. Chili pepper lowers cholesterol and turmeric also reduces inflammation pain.

Amy: My friend convinced me that there are herbs and spices that can help with depression and mood swings too. He assured me that he feels so much more energetic and positive when he includes certain foods in his diet.
Peter: That's amazing! So, what can we make that has all these ingredients in it? Let's make a super-healthy cure-all! Vanessa, you can chop up and prepare the ingredients and Amy can cook and stir and I'll add the spices and herbs!
Vanessa: Hold on there, Peter. Have you heard the expression, “There are too many cooks in the kitchen.”? It's a recipe for disaster!
